docs.title: 🚀 Welcome to Nestify Documentation
docs.text: Nestify is a fast, lightweight, and cross-platform CLI tool written in Go to scan, analyze, and generate project structures.

docs.title: 🧠 Analyze Command (nestify analyze)
docs.text:
The analyze command evaluates the overall structure of your project directory. It strips out build artifacts using .nestifyignore, calculates source-code language distribution based on real files, and aggregates directory metrics (file counts, folder counts, and total size).

It also outputs a compact, prompt-ready JSON summary intended for immediate copy-pasting into Large Language Model (LLM) workflows.

docs.title: 🛠️ Usage & Options
docs.text: nestify analyze [options]

docs.title: Flags & Options
docs.text:
Flag Short Description Default --path -p Target directory path to analyze. . (Current Directory) --depth -d Limits directory analysis depth (0 for unlimited). 0

Cross-Platform & Shell Agnostic

Nestify is compiled into a single native binary with zero external dependencies. All CLI commands run identically across Windows (PowerShell / CMD), macOS, and Linux (Bash / Zsh). Learn more about Shell Agnostic Execution.

docs.title: 1. Analyze Current Working Directory
docs.text:
Evaluates the current project layout and saves the report to Nestify-Report/skeleton_report.md.

nestify analyze

docs.title: 2. Limit Traversal Depth
docs.text:
Restricts analysis and language breakdown to top-level project directories up to depth level 2.

nestify analyze -d 2

docs.title: 3. Analyze External Project Path
docs.text:
Targets any external repository path without navigating away from your working directory.

nestify analyze --path ./projects/MyDotNetApp -d 3

docs.title: 📄 Output Overview (skeleton_report.md)
docs.text: When nestify analyze finishes running, it creates a structured report inside the Nestify-Report/ folder containing project metrics, visual language progress bars, and a prompt-ready JSON summary.

docs.title: ⚙️ Language Breakdown Logic
docs.text: Nestify scans file extensions throughout your project while adhering strictly to .nestifyignore. By suppressing heavy third-party dependencies (node_modules/, vendor/, bin/, obj/), the language statistics accurately reflect your custom codebase composition rather than generated or external code.

docs.title: 💬 AI Context Generation (nestify context)
docs.text:
The context command is Nestify's primary tool for Prompt Engineering and LLM Contextualization. It merges project metrics, source code language breakdowns, and directory tree representations into a single, unified Markdown file (Nestify-Report/ai_context_report.md).

Additionally, it allows developers to inject pre-built or custom prompt instructions directly into the top of the report, making it instantly ready to send to LLMs like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.

docs.title: 🛠️ Usage & Options
docs.text: nestify context [options]

docs.title: Flags & Options
docs.text:
Flag Short Description Default --prompt -p Injects an embedded prompt template (e.g. architecture, refactor, security) or raw instruction text into the report header. "" (None) --depth -d Limits directory tree traversal depth (0 for unlimited). 0 --path Target directory path to process. . (Current Directory)

Cross-Platform & Shell Agnostic

Nestify is compiled into a single native binary with zero external dependencies. All CLI commands run identically across Windows (PowerShell / CMD), macOS, and Linux (Bash / Zsh). Learn more about Shell Agnostic Execution.

docs.title: 🔍 Discovering & Inspecting Prompt Templates
docs.text:
Before injecting a prompt template into nestify context, you can discover available presets or preview their exact text using the built-in prompt management tools:

  • List all embedded prompt templates: 

    nestify prompt-list

  • Inspect a specific prompt's instruction text: 

    nestify prompt architecture

For full details on using and customizing prompt instructions, check out the Prompt Management Guide.

docs.title: 1. Generate Standard AI Context (No Injected Prompt)
docs.text:
Scans the current project, analyzes language breakdown, builds the folder tree, and exports ai_context_report.md.

nestify context

docs.title: 2. Inject Built-in Prompt Template with Depth Restriction
docs.text:
Uses the embedded architecture prompt template and restricts tree depth to 3 levels deep.

nestify context -p architecture -d 3

(Available embedded prompts can be discovered using nestify prompt-list).

docs.title: 3. Inject Custom Prompt Text Directly
docs.text:
Passes a custom task instruction directly from your terminal CLI session:

nestify context -p "Review this codebase structure for Go clean architecture guidelines" -d 3

docs.title: 🤖 Prompt Processing Resolution Order
docs.text:
When you use the -p or --prompt flag, Nestify resolves the prompt input using the following logic:

  1. Embedded Template Match: It checks whether the string matches an embedded template file inside templates-prompts/ (e.g., refactor, security, architecture)[cite: 6]. If a match is found, the template's file content is injected[cite: 6].
  2. Raw Text Fallback: If no template name matches the provided argument, Nestify treats the input as raw custom prompt text and injects it as-is into the header[cite: 6].

docs.title: 🚫 Ignore Management (ignore-list & ignore-use)
docs.text:
The Ignore System is the cornerstone of Nestify's noise-reduction engine. Before generating architecture reports or sending context to Large Language Models (LLMs), filtering out build artifacts, compiled binaries, dependency directories, and temporary OS files is critical to preserve token efficiency and report clarity.

Nestify provides embedded, zero-configuration ignore templates for 18+ major tech stacks.

docs.title: 🛠️ Commands Reference
docs.text: Nestify offers two primary commands to inspect and apply ignore templates:

docs.title: 1. List Available Templates (ignore-list)
docs.text:
Displays all tech-stack ignore templates built directly into the Nestify binary.

nestify ignore-list

docs.title: 2. Apply a Template (ignore-use)
docs.text:
Copies the specified embedded template into a local .nestifyignore file in your current working directory.

nestify ignore-use <template-name>

Cross-Platform & Shell Agnostic

Nestify is compiled into a single native binary with zero external dependencies. All CLI commands run identically across Windows (PowerShell / CMD), macOS, and Linux (Bash / Zsh). Learn more about Shell Agnostic Execution.

Run ignore-list to see available technology presets (e.g., go, dotnet, nodejs, python, flutter, unity, etc.):

docs.title: ⚙️ How .nestifyignore Works
docs.text: When any scanning command (scan, analyze, or context) is executed, Nestify looks for a .nestifyignore file in the project root. It parses gitignore-style glob patterns to exclude matching paths during directory traversal.

docs.title: Example .nestifyignore File Content (dotnet template):
docs.text:
# Build outputs
bin/
obj/
out/

# Dependencies & IDEs
.vs/
.vscode/
*.user
*.suo

# Test results
TestResults/

docs.title: 📝 Customizing Local Ignore Rules
docs.text:
The created .nestifyignore file is a plain text file. You can open it in any text editor and append project-specific custom rules:

# Append custom internal logs or data folders
/data/local_cache/
*.tmp_log
Default Scanning Behavior

If no .nestifyignore file is present in your target directory, Nestify performs a full, unfiltered traversal and includes all files and folders in the generated report. To ignore build artifacts or system clutter, ensure you generate a .nestifyignore file using nestify ignore-use <template>.

docs.title: 🏗️ Project Generation (nestify init)
docs.text:
The init command is Nestify's scaffolding engine. It reads a JSON layout blueprint and physically creates the entire directory and file hierarchy on your file system.

It can be used with embedded project presets or with JSON reports generated by nestify scan to instantly clone directory architectures.

docs.title: 🛠️ Usage & Options
docs.text: nestify init [options]

docs.title: Flags & Options
docs.text:
Flag Short Description Default --template -t Path to the JSON structure template or blueprint file. Required --path -p Target destination folder where the structure should be scaffolded. . (Current Directory)

Cross-Platform & Shell Agnostic

Nestify is compiled into a single native binary with zero external dependencies. All CLI commands run identically across Windows (PowerShell / CMD), macOS, and Linux (Bash / Zsh). Learn more about Shell Agnostic Execution.

docs.title: 1. Bootstrap Project from Embedded/Local Template
docs.text:
Scaffolds a standard Go project structure into a target directory (./MyNewApp):

nestify init --template templates-projects/go_standard.json --path ./MyNewApp

docs.title: 2. Architectural Reverse-Engineering (Scaffold from Existing Scan)
docs.text:
Recreate an empty directory layout blueprint captured from a scanned GitHub repository or existing project:

# Step 1: Scan an existing project folder-only
nestify scan --path ./ExistingApp --folders-only

# Step 2: Use the generated JSON report to create a brand new empty clone
nestify init --template Nestify-Report/ExistingApp_20260805_010000.json --path ./NewCleanApp

docs.title: 📋 JSON Template Structure Format
docs.text: The init command parses JSON blueprints built as nested node trees. Each object specifies a name, a type ("folder" or "file"), and an optional list of children nodes.

docs.title: Example JSON Blueprint (go_basic.json):
docs.text:
[
  {
    "name": "cmd",
    "type": "folder",
    "children": [
      {
        "name": "app",
        "type": "folder",
        "children": [
          {
            "name": "main.go",
            "type": "file"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "internal",
    "type": "folder",
    "children": [
      {
        "name": "config",
        "type": "folder"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "README.md",
    "type": "file"
  }
]

docs.title: ⚙️ How Generation Works
docs.text:
1. Path Normalization: Nestify automatically normalizes OS-specific path slashes (/ vs \) for seamless cross-platform execution.
  2. Recursive Directory Creation: It creates parent folders first before generating nested subdirectories or empty placeholder files.
  3. Safe Execution: Existing files are preserved unless overwritten, preventing accidental data loss during scaffolding.
Creating Custom Templates

You can create your own custom JSON blueprints manually or save nestify scan outputs to build a library of reusable organization templates.

docs.title: 🛠️ CLI Commands Overview
docs.text:
Nestify provides a suite of fast, token-efficient, and cross-platform command-line tools designed to streamline project structure scanning, codebase analysis, AI context generation, and project scaffolding[cite: 5].

All commands execute locally with zero network telemetry and share consistent syntax across Windows, macOS, and Linux[cite: 5].

docs.title: ⚡ Recommended Workflow Sequence
docs.text:
To get the most out of Nestify, follow this standard execution order:

graph LR
    A[<b>1. Suppress Clutter</b><br/><code>nestify ignore-use <tech></code>] --> B{Choose Your Goal}

    B -->|AI Context & Prompts| C[<b>AI Analysis</b><br/><code>nestify context -p <prompt></code>]
    B -->|Directory Tree & JSON| D[<b>Visual Scan</b><br/><code>nestify scan --tree</code>]
    B -->|Language Breakdown| E[<b>Code Metrics</b><br/><code>nestify analyze</code>]

  1. Suppress Clutter First: Run nestify ignore-use <tech-stack> to filter out compiled binaries, dependencies, and temporary files (bin/, obj/, node_modules/).

  2. Contextualize for AI: Run nestify context -p <template> to generate a complete codebase context report merged with custom LLM task instructions.

  3. Inspect Architecture: Run nestify scan --tree -d 2 to review high-level directory organization without drowning in file details.

docs.title: 🌐 Cross-Platform Parity
docs.text:
Nestify is compiled into a single native binary using Go. It requires no external runtime dependencies (Node.js, Python, or .NET).

Terminal & Shell Support

All syntax, flags, and outputs function identically across Windows (PowerShell, Command Prompt), macOS (Terminal, iTerm), and Linux (Bash, Zsh). File paths are automatically normalized across OS-specific separators (/ vs \).

docs.title: 💬 Prompt Management (prompt-list & prompt)
docs.text:
Nestify comes with a set of embedded, pre-built Prompt Templates designed for common LLM codebase analysis tasks (e.g., Clean Architecture checks, refactoring guides, security audits, and desktop app code reviews).

The prompt management commands allow you to discover available embedded prompts and inspect their exact text directly from your terminal.

docs.title: 1. List Available Prompts (prompt-list)
docs.text:
Displays all prompt templates built directly into the Nestify binary.

nestify prompt-list

docs.title: 2. View Prompt Content (prompt)
docs.text:
Prints the full instruction text of a specific embedded prompt template to the console.

nestify prompt <template-name>

Cross-Platform & Shell Agnostic

Nestify is compiled into a single native binary with zero external dependencies. All CLI commands run identically across Windows (PowerShell / CMD), macOS, and Linux (Bash / Zsh). Learn more about Shell Agnostic Execution.

docs.title: Step 1: List Built-in Prompt Templates
docs.text:
Run prompt-list to view all available prompt presets:

nestify prompt-list

Output Preview:

Available embedded prompt templates:
  - architecture
  - default
  - desktop
  - refactor
  - security

docs.title: Step 2: Inspect a Template's Content
docs.text:
Before injecting a prompt template into nestify context, you can preview its exact wording:

nestify prompt architecture

Output Preview:

You are an enterprise software architect experienced in Clean Architecture, Onion Architecture, and Event-Driven systems.
Evaluate the directory and module structure of this project.
Verify layer separation (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Presentation), check for dependency inversion violations, and suggest structural corrections to strictly maintain architectural boundaries.

docs.title: Step 3: Inject In AI Context Output
docs.text:
Once you know the name of your desired template, pass it to the context command using the -p flag:

nestify context -p architecture -d 2

docs.text: Template Name Primary Focus / Use Case architecture Evaluates Clean Architecture, Onion Architecture, and layer boundaries. refactor Identifies code smell indicators, monolithic folder coupling, and modularization targets. security Audits folder layouts for sensitive data exposure, config leaks, and unsafe path structures. desktop Analyzes client/desktop application components and UI architecture. default General codebase structure review for high-level AI analysis.

docs.title: 🔍 Scan Command (nestify scan)
docs.text: The scan command is the core structural scanner of Nestify. It recursively traverses a project directory, applies .nestifyignore rules to strip out build clutter and binary artifacts, and generates structured outputs in both JSON and Markdown Tree formats.

docs.title: 🛠️ Usage & Options
docs.text: nestify scan [options]

docs.title: Flags & Options
docs.text:
Flag Short Description Default --path -p Target directory path to scan. . (Current Directory) --tree Generates a human-readable ASCII tree report (.md). false --folders-only Restricts traversal to directories, ignoring all files. false --depth -d Limits directory traversal depth (0 for unlimited). 0

Cross-Platform & Shell Agnostic

Nestify is compiled into a single native binary with zero external dependencies. All CLI commands run identically across Windows (PowerShell / CMD), macOS, and Linux (Bash / Zsh). Learn more about Shell Agnostic Execution.

docs.title: 1. Basic Directory Scan (JSON Output)
docs.text:
Scans the current working directory and saves a timestamped JSON node report inside (Nestify-Report/).

nestify scan

docs.title: 2. Generate a Visual Directory Tree
docs.text:
Produces both the default JSON report and a clean ASCII tree Markdown report (Nestify-Report/PROJECT_TIMESTAMP.md).

nestify scan --tree

docs.title: 3. High-Level Clean Architecture View
docs.text:
Excludes files from the scan to inspect only the folder hierarchy up to a depth level of 2.

nestify scan --folders-only -d 2

docs.title: 4. Scan a Specific External Path
docs.text:
Target any folder on your file system without leaving your current terminal working directory.

nestify scan --path ./projects/MyApi --tree -d 3

docs.title: 🔒 Ignore Logic Integration
docs.text:
The scan command automatically respects:

  1. Standard built-in default ignore patterns (.git/, .DS_Store, etc.).
  2. Project-level .nestifyignore files located in the target scanning directory.
Need to ignore language-specific build folders?

Run nestify ignore-use <tech-stack> before scanning to automatically suppress heavy folders like node_modules/, bin/, obj/, or vendor/.
